title: Move a 2-inch wafer with tweezers from between its neighbours in one cassette into the empty slot of another
instruction: With the wafer tweezers standing in the stand on your left, take the middle wafer of the three in the near cassette and put it into the empty slot between the two wafers in the far cassette. Hold the wafer only with the tweezers, by its top edge, and lower it until it rests in the slot before you let go of it. Then stand the tweezers back in their stand, tips down, and let go of them. Do not touch or move any other wafer.
context: Wafers are moved between cassettes by hand with tweezers in university and pilot-line cleanrooms ("Transfer your wafers with tweezers into a clean carrier boat", UT Dallas cleanroom, spin rinse dryer procedure). Unlike picking up a wafer lying flat, the wafer stands upright in the cassette and has to come out of one slot and go into another between neighbours only 4.76 mm apart, holding a 0.28 mm-thick, 1.3 g disc by its edge with a sprung two-leaf tool.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases, on the table (x forward, y left). Two Chung King PP-C050 2-inch wafer cassettes (natural polypropylene, 14.2 cm long, 6.74 cm wide, 6.15 cm tall, 25 slots at 4.76 mm), standing upright with the open top up and the slots running left to right (the 14.2 cm length along y): the near cassette's footprint centred at x 22, y 15, the far one at x 30, y 15 (1.3 cm apart). Slot 1 is each cassette's right-hand end; slot k's centre is at y = 9.30 + 0.476 (k - 1). Five 2-inch silicon wafers (50.8 mm, 0.279 mm thick, 1.32 g) stand upright, fully down, in slots; the layout depends on the trial number k (k mod 3): A: near cassette slots 8, 9, 10 (move 9), far cassette slots 12 and 14 (target 13); B: near 12, 13, 14 (move 13), far 16 and 18 (target 17); C: near 16, 17, 18 (move 17), far 8 and 10 (target 9). Wafer tweezers: Ted Pella PELCO 5048-SV (13.65 cm long, stainless steel with carbon-fibre PVDF points 6 x 0.7 mm), standing tips down in a printed PLA stand (block 3.0 (x) x 5.4 (y) x 1.2 cm tall with a 1.6 x 1.8 cm through slot) centred at x 22, y 33, the leaves parting left-right. Nothing else is on the table. The cassettes and the stand are fixed (taped down).
scoring: Judged at the end of the trial (or once 1.0 has held for 1 s) from a photo, a ruler and the trial video. No credit while the tweezers hold the wafer: any score counts only once the tweezer tips are open and at least 5 cm from it. 1.0: the moved wafer stands in the target slot (the empty one in the far cassette: both of its edges in that slot's grooves, within 5 degrees of upright), fully down (its top edge within 2 mm of its neighbours' top edges), and the tweezers stand tips down in their stand with the robot at least 3 cm from them. 0.75: the same, but the tweezers are not back in the stand or the robot still touches them. 0.5: the wafer stands in the target slot but its top edge is more than 2 mm above its neighbours'. 0 otherwise, including a wafer in any other slot, across two slots, or still in the tweezers. Zero for the whole trial, whatever follows: the wafer falls free of the tweezers (a release above its resting place: a drop of 2 mm or more), any other wafer moves or rises 2 mm or more, or the moved wafer touches the table.
reset_notes: Put the five wafers in the slots of the next trial's layout (setup), fully down, and stand the tweezers tips down in their stand with the leaves parting left-right. Nothing is consumed.
fidelity: Wafers are drawn 0.5 mm thick (real 0.279 mm) at their real 1.32 g: at 0.279 and 0.4 mm a pinched wafer slipped or chattered out of the tweezers in the simulator; wafers and tweezer leaves have a capped depenetration speed (0.02 m/s). Rib shape, rail height and the tweezers' leaf section, spring (about 1 N to close) and mass are assumptions (README). Cassettes and stand are fixed; the tweezers are two rigid leaves on a sprung hinge; friction alone holds the wafer.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0; demo: 1.0 (layouts A, B and C, three runs each)
